description: A ground-level photograph captures an expansive wetland landscape under an overcast sky. The foreground shows a narrow strip of terrestrial ground covered with sparse, dry vegetation and what appears to be leaf litter. This transitions into a broad expanse of standing water, which dominates the mid-ground. Numerous clusters and larger patches of tall, dry, yellowish-brown grasses and sedges emerge from the water, with some vegetation partially submerged. In the middle distance, additional vegetated landforms, possibly small islands, are visible, interrupting the water surface. A distinct line of dark, deciduous trees forms the distant horizon, suggesting the edge of the wetland or a riparian zone. The image depicts a characteristic marsh or flooded grassland environment, consistent with areas described as "Marshes (freshwater or salt) with or without vegetation (reeds) coverage" or "Grasslands highly wet or flooded at least six months a year" within Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) documentation.
